title: Emergencies & Health
description: Learn essential English for emergency and health situations

explain.ta: அவசர மற்றும் சுகாதார சூழ்நிலைகளில் ஆங்கிலம் பேசுவது மிக முக்கியம். மருத்துவரிடம் பேசுவது, அவசர உதவி கேட்பது, அறிகுறிகளை விவரிப்பது போன்ற சூழ்நிலைகளுக்கு தயாராக இருங்கள். முக்கிய சொற்றொடர்கள்: 'I need help!', 'Please call an ambulance', 'I'm not feeling well', 'Where is the nearest hospital?'. தெளிவாக பேசுவது அவசர சூழ்நிலைகளில் உதவும்.
explain.en: Speaking English in emergency and health situations is crucial. Be prepared for situations like talking to doctors, asking for emergency help, and describing symptoms. Key phrases: 'I need help!', 'Please call an ambulance', 'I'm not feeling well', 'Where is the nearest hospital?'. Speaking clearly helps in emergency situations.

examples: I've been sick for two days.
How often should I take this?

examples.en: Help! Please call an ambulance. There's been an accident.
I'm not feeling well. I have a fever and headache.
examples.ta: எனக்கு உடல்நிலை சரியில்லை. காய்ச்சல் மற்றும் தலைவலி உள்ளது.

examples.en: Where is the nearest hospital? It's an emergency.
I've been sick for two days. I have stomach pain and nausea.
examples.ta: இரண்டு நாட்களாக உடல்நிலை சரியில்லை. வயிற்று வலி மற்றும் குமட்டல் உள்ளது.

examples.en: I need medicine for cold and cough. Do I need a prescription?
examples.ta: சளி மற்றும் இருமலுக்கு மருந்து தேவை. மருந்து சீட்டு தேவையா?

examples.en: How often should I take this medicine?
examples.ta: இந்த மருந்தை எத்தனை முறை எடுக்க வேண்டும்?

examples.en: I'm allergic to penicillin. Please note that.
examples.ta: எனக்கு பென்சிலின் ஒவ்வாமை உள்ளது. தயவுசெய்து குறித்துக்கொள்ளுங்கள்.

examples.en: I feel dizzy and I can't breathe properly.
examples.ta: தலை சுற்றுகிறது மற்றும் சரியாக சுவாசிக்க முடியவில்லை.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Good morning. What brings you here today?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: I'm not feeling well. I have a fever and headache.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: How long have you been feeling this way?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: For about two days now.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you have any other symptoms? Cough, body pain?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Yes, I have body pain and a slight cough.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: I'll prescribe some medicine. Take rest and drink plenty of fluids.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Thank you, doctor. How often should I take the medicine?

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Three times a day after meals. Come back if you don't feel better in three days.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Hello, I need medicine for cold and cough.

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.text: Do you have a prescription?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: No, I don't. Can I get something over the counter?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.text: Yes, I can give you this cough syrup and these tablets.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: How often should I take them?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.text: The syrup twice a day, and the tablets three times a day after meals.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Are there any side effects?

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.text: The syrup may cause drowsiness. Don't drive after taking it.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Hello! I need help! There's been an accident.

lines.speaker: Emergency Operator
lines.text: Stay calm. What is your location?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: I'm on MG Road, near the bus stop.

lines.speaker: Emergency Operator
lines.text: Is anyone injured?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Yes, one person is injured. They're conscious but in pain.

lines.speaker: Emergency Operator
lines.text: An ambulance is on the way. Stay with the person and keep them calm.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Okay, thank you. Please hurry.
